rationale: Both preserve language structure in machine-readable representations while requiring original forms and metadata to remain distinct from normalized analytical layers.
Both convert heterogeneous historical observations into modern searchable digital representations while requiring source provenance to remain attached.
The sea-ice record explicitly transitions from historical observations to satellite passive microwave data; Sentinel-1D adds a new SAR observation lineage for future Earth-surface analysis.
Both preserve long-lived instrument-derived time series whose calibration and instrument context are essential to later reanalysis.
Both depend on preserving instrument configuration, measurement context, preprocessing, and provenance to make downstream models interpretable and reproducible.
Both demonstrate why physical/digital collection identities and historical subcollections must survive migration into new discovery systems.
Both benefit from preserving original text artifacts separately from modern indexing, normalization, and search representations.
Both are current-generation additions to long-running Earth-observation measurement lineages where acquisition and processing metadata are critical to future reanalysis.
